newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's Aug trade deficit at monthly record high.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's Aug trade deficit at monthly record high.

text.p: South Korea's customs-cleared trade deficit widened to a monthly record high of $2.9 billion in August from a $901 million shortfall a year earlier, provisional figures released by the trade ministry showed on Monday.
NOTE: in millions of dollars, July figures revised
A trade ministry report attributed the deficit to a 52 percent year-on-year fall in semiconducter exports in August. Exports of chips dropped to $1.02 billion from $2.12 billion a year earlier.
Semiconductors are the biggest single item of South Korean exports and their price has plummeted on world markets, hurting the overall economy.
The international spot price for 16-megabit dynamic random access memory (DRAM) chips fell to $12 per unit in August from $50.1 a year ago, the report said.
Imports rose 11.7 percent to $12.86 billion in August from $11.52 billion a year ago, the report said.
The steady increase in imports was attributed mostly to the strong 30.3 percent year-on-year growth in imports of consumer goods, it said.
The trade deficit for the first eight months of this year widened to $13.29 billion from an $8.75 billion shortfall the previous year, the ministry report said.
Semiconductor exports for the January-August period were down 4.2 percent to $12.44 billion this year from $12.99 billion a year ago.
Exports of all other items posted a 9.6 percent rise to $72.73 billion from $66.36 billion last year.
Imports for the eight months were up 11.8 percent to $98.45 billion from $88.09 billion in the same period last year.
Letters of credit received during the first 20 days of August fell eight percent year-on-year to $3.08 billion, the ministry report said.
Import licenses issued during the same 20-day period rose 11.5 percent year-on-year to $6.4 billion, it said.
